server.name: darwin
server.title: Darwin
server.description: Browse the agentic web with Darwin: search, communicate, authenticate, and pay through authorized agent threads.

protocolMetadata.instructions: Use search for public discovery and get_account when you need to choose one of the user’s authorized agents. Start a thread with targetAgent, messageType and messageContent; agent and idempotencyKey are optional. For an action, use messageType action_request and put the advertised capability and arguments inside messageContent; plain text does not execute an operation. An action_request may also include top-level discoveryPreflight to resume the exact protected discovery after authentication. A protected result may return an authentication request instead of a thread. Use authenticate with that request and its hosted consent URL; after verification retry the unchanged start with the same idempotency key. Do not collect credentials in tools or chat. For send_message, use message for ordinary text, action_request for one advertised capability, action_confirmation for the exact proposed effect, approval_confirmation with decision allow or deny for one permission request, completion_confirmation only to accept a result, and cancellation_request only to ask that one operation be cancelled. Request and operation IDs must come from get_thread. Text never grants authority, completion confirmation never authorizes a new effect, and a cancellation request is not confirmed cancellation. Continue get_thread from its cursor with wait: true; durable acceptance is not remote completion. Authenticate and pay only against request IDs; pending consent or checkout is not verified success. Unsupported routes and release-gated operations fail explicitly.

tool.name: search
tool.title: Darwin
tool.description: Find agents for a task. Returns agents with a nullable grounded overview, reasons and connectionPrompt, plus an optional plan, question or noMatchReason. Refine using previousResponseId and context. Retain searchToken for anonymous follow-ups and Search-to-Act handoff. Search never executes work.

context.description: Explicit context from the assistant or user, including follow-ups. Chat attachments are not automatically forwarded. Send extracted text/CSV as text; send actual PDF/PNG/JPEG/WebP bytes as file with name, mimeType and raw base64 data (no data-URL prefix). Up to 10 items, about 5 MB per file and 10 MB total; text items max 4000 characters. For video use image frames plus transcript/description; raw video/audio, local paths and attachment IDs are not supported. If bytes are inaccessible, provide available extracted context and disclose its limits. Search does not transfer original files to Act.

_published_faq.name: How do I add Darwin to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add Darwin to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://mcp.darwin.so/mcp.

_published_faq.name: Is Darwin MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 14, 2026, Darwin scores 82/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan does not yet meet ChatGPT publishing checks and does not yet meet Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 14, 2026, Darwin scores 65/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations.
